column1: # Status of each BEAUti combination, for the status page (scripts/build_status_page.py).
# Columns: ID <TAB> status <TAB> note. Notes may use `code` and **bold**.
#   pass       matched, no flags, full chains
#   explained  flagged only because of a known, explained difference
#   partial    matched, but most runs stopped before the end of the chain
#   rerun      needs rerunning (rc1 build, or a flag to recheck with new seeds)
#   blocked    needs a build with a fix made after rc2 (rc3)
#   fail       not matched, difference not explained yet
#   none       no results in the repo yet
# Min ESS, max z and the script's verdict come from reports/summary/batch-summary.md;
# tester and model come from ASSIGNMENTS.md.

column3: All defaults. Largest z just under the flag.
Rerun on rc2; BEAST 2 replicate 2 extended (10 Nov): matched, smallest ESS 296.
Full 30M chains (Yuan, 9 Nov). Clades from the 8 Nov tree files, some of which end before 30M.
Four replicates. `prior` offset is the known 0.1 per gamma shape. `gammaShape.2ndpos` z = 3.2 pooled, within the replicate-to-replicate noise; seeds 3–4 alone pass.
Crashes at start in rc1 and rc2 (NPE in `CalibratedYuleModel`). Fixed by beast3#198. Sophie's rc2 XML runs on master.
Rerun on rc2.

Rerun on rc2 (10 Nov): the gamma shape is now bounded at 0.1 and matches (0.120 vs 0.118). Still not matched because the clock-rate priors differ: BEAST 2 has LogNormal(1, 1.25), BEAST 3 the default Gamma(0.01, 100), which shifts the clock rate (z = 61), tree height and `prior`. Rebuild the BEAST 2 side with the default Gamma(0.01, 100) clock prior and rerun it; both BEAST 2 runs also stopped before the end of the chain.
Versions agree, but both have the `SampleOffValues` Hastings bug. Needs rc3 and a BEAST.base 2.7.9 refresh.

Compared by clade from the trees (`Indicators.N` is indexed by node number, not clade): all branch rates match. Runs extended to 100M; BEAST 2 rep2 stopped at 76.7M. Branch-rate rows still use the shorter tree files until Yuan's new ones are in Dropbox.

The priors differ: BEAST 3 has Gamma(0.01, 100) on the mean clock rate, BEAST 2 none (improper flat). Clock rate and every branch rate are 0.4% lower in BEAST 3 (z ≈ 3–5); clades match. BEAUti 2.7 can't add the prior (template bug, [BeastFX#114](https://github.com/CompEvol/BeastFX/pull/114)), and BEAUti 3 rc2 doesn't offer a Uniform for a positive parameter ([beast3#217](https://github.com/CompEvol/beast3/issues/217)). [beast3#224](https://github.com/CompEvol/beast3/pull/224), merged after rc2, adds NonNegativeUniform: on rc3, rebuild the BEAST 3 side with **NonNegativeUniform(0, 10)** on the mean clock rate and every other prior set to match the 2.7.9 XML (rc3's BEAUti defaults differ, #208), keep the BEAST 2 XML as it is, and rerun both. Trace logs are in Dropbox (58–68 MB).
Full 35M chains (Yuan, 9 Nov). ORC relaxed clock matches. Clades from the 8 Nov tree files, some of which end before 35M.
Rebuilt on rc2 with ORC's `BranchRatePrior` linked to `ORCsigma` (10 Nov): matches, `ORCsigma` z = 2.2, clades match (max Δp 0.026).
`prior` z = 9.1: the gamma-shape normalisation offset (0.1). Posterior unaffected.
Rerun on rc2 (10 Nov): matched (max z 1.14, clades match, max Δp 0.005).
The priors differ: BEAST 2 has Uniform(0, ∞) on the Yule birth rate, BEAST 3 Gamma(0.01, 100), so `prior`, `birthRate` and the tree height differ. Rebuild with the same birth-rate prior and rerun.
Run on rc2 with `data/anolis-start.newick`; BEAST 2 replicate 1 extended (10 Nov): matched, smallest ESS 273.
Full 100M chains (Yuan, 9 Nov). All four unlinked trees match. Clades from the 8 Nov tree files, some of which end before 100M.
Every marginal also matches its analytic prior.
`CalibratedYuleModel` z = 8.2 is a logging difference. Both match U(4, 6) and U(8, 10).

Eva's 2.7.9 XMLs run in BEAST 3 rc2 match her 2.7.9 runs (C06 max z 2.3; C10 max z 2.4). In C10 the frequencies mix about 4× worse in BEAST 3 than in 2.7.9 (ESS 107 vs about 420 per replicate) with the legacy classes; BEAST 3's own C10 XML reaches 2803. BEAUti 3 can't open 2.7 XML; [beast3#229](https://github.com/CompEvol/beast3/pull/229) makes it say so.
Full 10M chains (Yuan, 9 Nov). Clades from the 8 Nov tree files, some of which end before 10M.
Full 20M chains (Yuan, 9 Nov). Resumed run matches the uninterrupted runs (max z 1.55).
